habitat: Forages over open country and woodland; breeds on tall cliffs (colonies May–Oct). In Kruger mainly a visitor/wanderer from escarpment colonies; often soars high and may perch on pylons (Newman's; SABAP1).
summary: A large, pale endemic African vulture. Adults are very pale brown to whitish on the body with dark flight feathers and a honey-coloured eye; immatures are warmer rufous-brown with pinker neck skin. Easily confused with White-backed Vulture where ranges overlap (Newman's).

similar.note: White-backed is smaller; adult has a contrasting white lower back (visible in flight from above); eye dark, not honey-coloured (Newman's).
Lappet-faced is darker-bodied with a massive bill and crimson bare head; white 'pants' in adults (Newman's).

research.note: Research confidence was medium-high and is stored as medium. No seasonal plumage change is described in the sources consulted, except presence/absence of migrants. Gaps: No juvenile/immature image in selected set. Photos left out: The file name says Cape Vulture but the description says White-backed Vulture (Gyps africanus), so the photo was left out. Colour phrases outside the vocabulary were stored as the nearest swatch: blue-grey to blue and grey; honey to gold; whitish to white.
